body.p: Tools that, once executed, cannot be undone or previewed by AI Positron are considered unsafe. These tools include all tools obtained through the Model Context Protocol integration and tools used to run command lines. By default, for such tools, the end user is explicitly asked in the chat box to allow the tool to run. When prompted, the end user can also choose to always allow a tool to run. In that case, the allowed tool is automatically added to the list of allowed tools on this preferences page.

The text area contains a line-separated list of entries for the tools that are always allowed to run without asking the end user. Each entry begins with a tool name, which must match exactly, unless it contains the * character. The * character acts as a wildcard that matches any sequence of characters.

For the command-line tool (run_command_line), the tool name can be followed by a space and a command key. The command key is a short, underscore-separated name that the AI model assigns to each command line. It describes the command line rather than repeating it. For example, the command line p4 opened //demo/spec/... may be assigned the p4_opened_demo_spec key. When the end user always allows a command line, an entry that consists of the tool name and command key, such as run_command_line p4_opened_demo_spec, is added to the list. This lets the end user always allow a specific command line while still being prompted about any other command line. The command key in an entry is matched as follows:

ul.li: Without a wildcard, the entry's command key must be identical to the command-line key. For example, run_command_line p4_opened allows the p4_opened key but not the p4_opened_demo_spec key.

With a wildcard, the entry's command key is a pattern that must match the entire command-line key. For example, run_command_line p4_opened_* allows every key that starts with p4_opened_, and run_command_line p4_* allows every key that starts with p4_.
Without a command key, the entry allows all command lines. This applies to both run_command_line and run_command_line*.

body.p: The AI model chooses the command key to describe the command line. The key does not restrict the command line itself. Because the AI model chooses the key, the same command line may receive a slightly different key in another run. Use a wildcard to cover these variations. The Always allow option is not available for a command line whose key contains the * character.

If you want to allow all tool calls to the MCP server, you can manually edit that entry to use the wildcard form brave-search_*.
An entry made only of * characters, or a command key made only of * characters, matches nothing, so it cannot allow every tool or every command line by accident.
This preferences page can be saved at project level if you want to share a certain set of allowed tools with your team members.
